_answersToYourFiveGaps._preamble: Three resolve inside §A2, one is a schedule-content problem rather than an engine one, and one is genuinely open and routed to the owner.
_answersToYourFiveGaps.1_multiplicityAcrossClasses: **Report, never suppress.** The mismatch is real and it is not the engine's to fix: `house.<component-type>` asks a CAPTURE-vocabulary question and a class is a DESK-vocabulary answer — Amendment 6's own distinction, arriving one level up. So a schedule item firing on a house whose only match is `sewage-ejector` is a **schedule content problem**, fixable in an inert file, and the engine's job is to surface it: *this item fired on type X; the classes present under X are [sewage-ejector]*. **That is a review-queue input, §7's third case.** Preserve, display, count, mark — never silently suppress.
_answersToYourFiveGaps.2_audienceHasNoEngineCounterpart: **Open, and routed to the owner rather than decided here.** Two fields in this territory were proposed and withdrawn on 2026-08-05, so this one gets stated rather than shipped. **The argument that distinguishes it: the schedule and the engine feed ONE list, and one of them declares an audience default. If the other does not, `s15.owner-pro-split` — a month-one required deliverable — is mostly blank, and the two halves of one list render differently in front of a client.** That is a consistency argument rather than a who-may-do-it argument, which is what killed the other two. Owner's call.
_answersToYourFiveGaps.3_zeroCareUnderARecurringSlot: **§A2 covers it and the wording could be clearer.** *The engine contributes identity and multiplicity inside the slot* does not require the engine to have CARE. `sump-discharge` contributes identity — which discharge, running where — to a winter slot the schedule owns. **Identity alone is a contribution**, and 50 of 173 classes are in that position.
_answersToYourFiveGaps.4_compositeTriggers: **The join is per-disjunct, not per-item.** An `any(...)` item joins on every component type it names and on nothing for its `property.*` disjuncts, so it is reachable by several classes and by none. Many-to-many rather than one-to-one, and **it fires once however many disjuncts match**, so no duplicate arises. §A1's join holds; it was stated for the simple case.
_answersToYourFiveGaps.5_theOverridePathIsUnreachable: **Correct, and no field is missing.** Frame §3 puts the interval on the RESEARCH PASS output, not on the care category — the class declares the category, AI supplies the interval per model. So §A2's override input is the research pass, which is unbuilt. **The mechanism is correctly specified and waits on Increment 5 rather than on a schema change.** Your decision not to write the scan is right and it is 11b: it would report green from birth.

careCategories.label: Sanitising
careCategories.note: Water coolers, ice makers, instant-hot dispensers. Standing water at room temperature — the care nobody does because nothing looks wrong.

careCategories.label: Firmware and account review
careCategories.note: Smart devices. A camera on abandoned firmware and an account nobody can log into are both failures, and neither is visible in the house.

careCategories.label: Blade cleaning and seasonal direction reversal
careCategories.note: Ceiling fans. The reversal is a real seasonal item and almost nobody does it.

careCategories.label: Caulk and grout renewal
careCategories.note: Not mechanical, and it is what stands between a shower and rot in the wall cavity.

careCategories.label: Monitoring contract review
careCategories.note: Security panels. The contract is the thing that fails, not the panel.

inspectionPoints.label: Alarm test and response
inspectionPoints.note: Pressing test proves the horn, not the sensor. Worth naming because the household believes it proves both.

inspectionPoints.label: Device age against its printed expiry
inspectionPoints.note: Smoke and CO alarms carry a hard replacement date printed on the housing — ten years for smoke, seven to ten for CO. **A date, not a judgement**, which is why this is the frame's cleanest inspection point.

inspectionPoints.label: Placement and coverage against requirement
inspectionPoints.note: One per storey, outside sleeping areas, and near fuel-burning equipment. A count against a requirement rather than a condition assessment.

inspectionPoints.label: Radon fan operation and manometer
inspectionPoints.note: A U-tube manometer with the fluid level even means the fan has stopped. Visible, unmistakable, and nobody knows to look.

inspectionPoints.label: Fan flow and termination
inspectionPoints.note: A bathroom fan that runs and vents into the attic is the moisture failure that hides best.

opportunityConditions.label: Alarm past its printed replacement date
opportunityConditions.note: A hard date rather than a judgement, which makes it the least arguable row in the frame.

opportunityConditions.label: Fuel-burning equipment with no CO alarm nearby
Extinguisher past its service or replacement date
Bathroom fan venting into the attic
opportunityConditions.note: The moisture failure that hides best — it looks like it is working from inside the room.

ownerQuestions.label: Have you tested them, and when?
Who monitors it, and is the contract current?
Can you still sign in to it?
ownerQuestions.note: Smart devices outlive their accounts. A camera nobody can reach is a device that is not there.

classes.label: Smoke alarm
classes.note: Ten-year replacement is a hard date printed on the housing, not a judgement — which makes this the cleanest row in the frame. Everything else here is a count against a requirement rather than a condition assessment, and that distinction is what keeps a concierge on the documenting side of the line.

classes.label: Carbon monoxide alarm
classes.note: Shares its checklist with the smoke alarm and its own expiry is shorter — seven to ten years rather than ten. Same shape, different date, which is exactly why it is a separate class.

classes.label: Fire extinguisher
classes.note: No checklist at v1.11.0, and a real inspection and recharge date. Its gauge is readable by anyone and read by nobody. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Radon mitigation fan
classes.note: Stub component type at v1.11.0. A U-tube manometer with its fluid level even means the fan has stopped — visible, unmistakable, and nobody knows to look. Zero care is a ruling.

classes.label: Bathroom exhaust fan
classes.note: Arguably belongs in heating and cooling — it is the moisture control that fails silently, and a fan that runs while venting into the attic looks like it is working from inside the room. Kept in tier two because it has no component type.

classes.label: Ceiling fan
classes.note: Seasonal direction reversal is a real item almost nobody does.

classes.label: Caulk and grout
classes.note: Not mechanical, and it is what stands between a shower and rot in the wall cavity. No replacement horizon — it is renewed on condition, forever.

classes.label: Water cooler

_modifiedClasses.label: Garburator
_modifiedClasses.note: DUPLICATE RESOLVED 2026-08-06, and the correction leads per rule 14. This class and v0.2's `garburator` are one thing under two names — it arrived from outside review as `food-waste-disposer` and shipped before the tier-two pass reached v0.2's own id. **The id stays `food-waste-disposer` because it is already shipped and referenced; the label becomes `Garburator` because that is what a household in this region says.** Common, real, and everyone abuses it — and it sits on the boundary between appliances and plumbing, filed under appliances because it is one.
